articles.title: Cavan Sullivan, Gio Reyna Named to USMNT Squad for International Matches, Full Roster Revealed
articles.summary: The United States men's national team and returning manager Mauricio Pochettino announced the full roster for upcoming friendlies against Peru and Chile, highlighted by 16-year-old ascending star Cavan Sullivan and midfielder Gio Reyna.
articles.body:
The United States men's national team and returning manager Mauricio Pochettino announced the full roster for upcoming friendlies against Peru and Chile, highlighted by 16-year-old ascending star Cavan Sullivan and midfielder Gio Reyna.

A number of prominent players will not feature, however, including Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie as they return to fitness.

Here's a look at the full roster and the schedule they'll face during the 16-day international break as the USMNT returns to play for the first time since reaching the Round of 16 at this summer's World Cup.

Christopher Brady, Chicago Fire FC (USA)

Sergiño Dest, PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands)

George Campbell, West Bromwich Albion F.C. (England)

Peyton Miller, New England Revolution (USA)

Chris Richards, Crystal Palace F.C. (England)

Frankie Westfield, Philadelphia Union (USA)

Sebastian Berhalter, Middlesbrough F.C. (England)

Gio Reyna, RC Strasbourg Alsace (France)

Brooklyn Raines, New England Revolution (USA)

Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia Union (USA)

Malik Tillman, Bayer 04 Leverkusen (Germany)

Ricardo Pepi, PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands)

Mathis Albert, Borussia Dortmund (Germany)

Zavier Gozo, Crystal Palace F.C. (England)

Saturday, Sept. 26 at 4:30 p.m. vs. Peru / Orlando's Inter.co Stadium (TNT)

Tuesday, Sept. 29 at 8 p.m. vs. Chile / St. Louis' Energizer Park (TNT)

Saturday, Oct. 3 at 10 p.m. vs. Mexico / Glendale (AZ)'s State Farm Stadium (TNT)

Tuesday, Oct. 6 at 8 p.m. vs. Canada / St. Paul's Allianz Field (TNT)

Much of the focus will be on Sullivan's inclusion, though it shouldn't come as much of a surprise—he's been thriving in MLS play and appears to be the next great superstar in United States soccer.

Sullivan now has five goals and six assists in his last seven MLS games and has been one of the most dynamic players in the entire league this season. His first call-up to the U.S. senior squad was only a matter of time, and Poch saw little reason to delay it any further.

Beyond that, Reyna will once again be available for Pochettino after his inclusion on the World Cup squad (and goal against Paraguay). Reyna's had a rocky enough relationship with the USMNT (and more than one club) that it's easy enough to forget that he's only 23 and still seemingly has his best football ahead of him.

Another notable inclusion is Musah, who was left off the World Cup roster after being a regular fixture for the USMNT, in large part down to a rough loan spell for Serie A's Atalanta last season. But the 23-year-old has looked much improved upon his return to AC Milan and will get another look from Pochettino.

But there is also plenty of youth on the roster, which doesn't come as much of a surprise given past comments from Pochettino.

"We were talking a lot in the last few weeks, the coaching staff, trying to open a new chapter and not make it a continuation of what happened in the last 18 or 19 months that we were working," he said in August after signing a new contract with the USMNT. "We were only focused on arriving at the World Cup in the best condition. Now the approach is going to be different, and it must be different, because it's a four-year cycle. It's a project that is about establishing different principles."

articles.title: Premier League predictions: Chris Sutton v legendary guitarist and Man City fan Johnny Marr - & AI
articles.summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on legendary guitarist and Man City fan Johnny Marr, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
articles.body:
The pressure is growing on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, but can his side sign off for the three-week international break by beating Fulham on Sunday?

"For teams who have had a bad start to the season, United being one of them, it could be a horrible few weeks," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Any negativity is going to just fester, really. There will be speculation about his future, along with all the talk about whether this is a good time to replace your manager.

"United are not the only team to have made a bad start, but there is a lot to ponder on for them at the moment. It makes this weekend even more important."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week four, he takes on legendary guitarist and Manchester City fan, Johnny Marr.

Marr's new album, The Age Of Everything, is out on 2 October.

Do you agree with their scores? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competitions.

Marr has enjoyed City's 100% start to the new Premier League season, with Sunday's win at Old Trafford continuing their impressive start under new boss Enzo Maresca.

"I think that derby will be remembered by City fans for a long time," Marr told BBC Sport.

"We all feared the worst when Phil Foden was sent off so early, because you don't know what could happen. It should have been a yellow card for him and Bruno Fernandes anyway.

"It's all a bit of a learning curve for the fans and the club with a new manager and so many new players, so to see how the team dug in and won was so great for City fans.

"No-one expected Maresca to win his first four games... but then again, why not? He's shown that he's his own man with his own philosophy. I like him."

Chris Sutton and Johnny Marr were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Chelsea are free-scoring and their front-line is so dynamic - but they are leaking goals left, right and centre and they are a bit of a rabble at the back.

I do think Chelsea will stop conceding eventually, but finding the right balance between defence and attack is Xabi Alonso's big problem at the moment because it is far too easy to create chances against his side.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews has got that balance in his team. They are very dangerous on the counter-attack, so you have to think they will hurt Chelsea too.

This fixture finished in a 2-2 draw in September last year, and I can see it going the same way this time.

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi has this reputation of being a great coach, and we saw what a good job he did at Brighton .

But we have not seen any improvement from Spurs yet, despite the big money they have spent, and he is surely going to come under pressure soon if their poor results continue.

They are not the only ones to revamp their squad but if you listen to De Zerbi, after about five years they might come good.

He keeps saying they need time, but he has had long enough for their results to be much better already. Other clubs, like Hull and Ipswich, have brought plenty of players in and are doing well enough - so why aren't Spurs?

I think De Zerbi has to come under scrutiny, but it is different with Unai Emery at Aston Villa .

They are also without a league win, but they look more likely to score goals, as they showed against Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

I am expecting Villa to improve the same way they did after not winning any of their first five games last season, and I can see them edging this.

Do I give Spurs their first league goal of the season? Yes, but only one. They are due a deflection, or Villa will score an own goal.

Something will go for them, but not the result.

There might be a bit of an edge to this one after Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had a pop at Arsenal over their time-wasting when they beat the Seagulls near the end of last season.

I love the way Brighton play and I was at Old Trafford to watch their comeback to beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday .

It doesn't seem to matter who they are missing from their team, Brighton are just bold as brass with the way they press and get men forward.

Luka Vuskovic, who they got from Spurs for £46m in the summer, is only 19 but he strolled through the game against United. What a player he looks.

The issue I have with Brighton in this game, however, is that Arsenal are not Manchester United . They are a cut above that.

Arsenal are the real deal and I don't see any weaknesses in their team, as their impressive win at Sunderland underlined. They are brave going forward, but they are also street-wise defensively and can see out a game when they have to, time-wasting or not.

They have that steel about them but I also think they could expose Brighton if Hurzeler's side go toe-to-toe with them, which is what I am expecting.

I nearly went for an Ipswich draw last week but changed my mind and went for Crystal Palace to win.

That meant I'd predicted Ipswich would lose their first four league games and they are joint-bottom of the table based on my predictions (see bottom of page).

Gary O'Neil's side have obviously done much better than that in reality - I know Palace went down to 10 men last week but, even so, well done to the Tractor Boys for finding a way to win that game.

Fair play to them, I like the ambition the club's owners have shown in the transfer market, and I really like the way O'Neil sets his team up. They are not just there to sit in in games, and they have got their reward.

I still fancy Everton to win this, though. They have made a great start to the season to stay unbeaten so far and, under David Moyes, they are a battle-hardened, resolute and well-organised outfit.

As a former Norwich striker I often get accused of being biased against Ipswich, but I am not being overly negative about them here.

I just see it being a tough afternoon for them, without getting a goal, and then a long trip home for Ipswich fans on the A14 - hopefully they don't close any of the major roads on Saturday so it is not an even more miserable journey back for them.

I can see this being a frustrating afternoon for Newcastle because they are going to come up against a Hull team who are brilliant at defending the box but are also brave with the way they throw people forward.

They are a threat from set-plays too but they have got the bit between their teeth and their whole attitude seems to be 'attack the Premier League' after getting promoted, which I really admire.

Along with Ipswich, Hull are the only other team I've predicted to lose all their games so far.

I am going to tip them not to lose this time... so you know what is probably going to happen. Apologies in advance to Tigers fans, because this happened with me and Sunderland last season.

Coventry were served up a couple of shockers by getting Arsenal and Manchester City as their first two away fixtures and this trip is far from easy for them either.

In fact this is another stinker of a game for Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard, because they are still struggling while Oliver Glasner seems to be getting Nottingham Forest going after a slow burner of a start.

There is a strong chance that Coventry's confidence has been sapped already so Lampard will be trying to rally the troops and give his players some belief that they can compete at this level.

That is going to be really difficult because they must be looking at the results of the other promoted teams and not just thinking 'where is a win coming from for us?' - but also 'where is a point coming from?', and 'where is a goal coming from?' too.

I don't think they will get any of those things this week, because Forest are looking pretty solid.

Well done to Forest striker Liam Delap by the way, who got his first goal for them in last week's win at Aston Villa .

He had a tough time at Chelsea , and I know what that is like, so it is great to see him off the mark for his new club.

By the way, Delap scored one league goal for Chelsea , same as me, but his price went up by £20m, from £30m to £50m.

My value went down by almost 50% when I left Stamford Bridge - from £10m to £6m - so what has gone on there?

Seriously, though, sometimes you need a change of scene to find your form again and Delap must be feeling a bit freer now he has his first Forest goal.

I am not convinced by Liverpool at all after covering them for Radio 5 Live last week - I thought Fulham were the better side in their 0-0 draw at Anfield.

Andoni Iraola's side did not flow in the final third, certainly not in the way his Bournemouth team did last season.

I don't think the Reds players are quite in sync with what Iraola is asking them to do in terms of their press either, and Fulham played through them with ease at times.

Marco Rose is an attacking manager so if Liverpool don't buck their ideas up then Bournemouth are going to do the same, and Iraola could end up losing on his return to his former club.

The one thing in Iraola's favour is that Bournemouth seem to be finding a way to draw games that they should win, so that is the result I am going with even though though I quite fancy the Cherries to take all three points.

I think I am in love with Leeds boss Daniel Farke. What a guy.

We were talking about him on the Monday Night Club before Leeds walloped Newcastle and only idiots question whether he is the right man to move the club forward now.

To see them beat Newcastle , and how emphatically they did it, was massive and more proof of their progress.

In contrast, Crystal Palace are almost on the precipice after their shaky start under new manager Pierre Sage, and I just don't see the Eagles getting anything here.

Leeds are so well organised at the back with new goalkeeper James Trafford, who is an upgrade on last season, and and a new centre-half I like too, in Tarik Muharemovic.

Apart from me, no-one else could say Muharemovic's name on the Monday Night Club, not even the posh Rory Smith, which I quite enjoyed.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is flying up front, as well. He is fit, motivated and a real handful, which is another reason I can't see past a Leeds victory.

Sunderland are a really good team and, on their day, they are more than a match for anyone.

The Black Cats are strong and robust, and when they get after teams and press you then they are phenomenal.

All of that makes me think this is a really hard game for Manchester City .

Their derby victory was a brilliant win and Maresca's biggest result as their manager so far, with the way they did it.

Iliman Ndiaye showed what a good signing he is when he came on for Rayan Cherki in the second half at Old Trafford, in terms of offering a different profile.

Cherki's more of an inside forward, as a number 10 or playing narrow, and he's a guy where you think you couldn't get the ball off him in a telephone box.

Ndiaye, though, will do more work going back and is also more of a ball carrier, so he was exactly what City needed when they went a man down.

United can feel hard done by because City's winner should have been disallowed, but City were the better team with 10 men.

This will be a very different task for Maresca's men, with the emphasis on them breaking down the Black Cats, but I don't feel it will just be one-way traffic.

I still think City will find a way though, and they need to for the sake of the title race. They already seem to be the only team capable of keeping pace with Arsenal .

Johnny on former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down in the summer, and his favourite City players: No-one expected Pep to stay for 10 years so it made him leaving OK to accept, and good luck to him. Aside from the success he brought to the club, City fans loved him because he totally loved Manchester.

Dennis Tueart was my favourite player when I was a kid and I think he could have played in this current era. We've had amazing players in the last 12 or so years so how do you pick, but my favourites would be Vincent Kompany, Sergio Aguero and David Silva, with the top place going to Kevin De Bruyne. I'd say he's the best player I've seen in a City shirt.

Watching Fulham draw at Anfield last weekend changed my view on them.

I had not seen Alvaro Arbeloa's side over 90 minutes before and, while their other results were poor, this time they were excellent.

They cut through Liverpool and had some nice patterns of play, but also defended well too. Arbeloa said afterwards that they played with more balance and I think that is a good way to describe their display.

Then I went to Manchester United 's defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and their performance was very poor.

Carrick really needs a response with a win here to take into the international break but how can I give United a chance, after the way the Seagulls absolutely dismantled them?

Three times in the past four seasons, United have gone to Craven Cottage and nicked the win late on, but I can't make a case for that happening.

As well as having problems up front, United are struggling defensively and I can see Fulham creating plenty of opportunities against them too.

Chris and his guest, Dorking Wanderers boss Marc White, both got four correct results with no exact scores from the 10 games in week four, giving them 40 points each.

AI did better, thanks to an exact score for Brentford 's 2-2 draw with Bournemouth which, along with two other correct results, gave it a total of 60 points.

But it was the collective efforts of the BBC readers who took the weekly win - their first of the season - that also sees them move from bottom to level on points with Chris at the top of the predictions table.

They also got one exact score - Arsenal 's 2-0 win at Sunderland - but also managed four correct results, giving them a total of 40 points.

It was a tough week for predictions, with only two games where everyone picked the right outcome - that victory for the Gunners, and Brighton 's win at Coventry.

There were five games where none of our predictors guessed the result - Nottingham Forest 's win at Aston Villa , Hull's draw at Chelsea , Ipswich's win at Crystal Palace , Fulham 's draw at Liverpool and Leeds ' win over Newcastle .

The biggest shock of the week came at Anfield. From more than 33,000 predictions, just under 30,000 (91%) of you went for a Liverpool win, while fewer than 2,000 of you went for any sort of draw and only 390 of you got the correct 0-0 scoreline.

articles.title: El Barça presume de una cifra goleadora de otra época
articles.standfirst: Para encontrar un registro mejor que el de los culés hay que remontarse al Sevilla de 1940
articles.summary: Para encontrar un registro mejor que el de los culés hay que remontarse al Sevilla de 1940
articles.body: Hacía 86 años que ningún equipo firmaba unos registros goleadores tan espectaculares como los que presenta ahora el Barcelona. El conjunto azulgrana ha convertido el inicio de temporada en una auténtica exhibición ofensiva y sus cifras ya le han permitido entrar en los libros de historia de LaLiga. Los seguidores culés están disfrutando de un equipo que llegó al verano con una carpeta pendiente sobre la mesa: quién ocuparía la posición de delantero centro tras la salida de Lewandowski y Ferran Torres. La respuesta, al menos hasta ahora, ha llegado de la mano de un Raphinha estelar, utilizado como falso '9' y convertido en una de las grandes referencias del equipo. Los números hablan por sí solos. El Barcelona ha celebrado 28 goles en las seis primeras jornadas de LaLiga, lo que supone una media de 4,6 tantos por partido. Una auténtica barbaridad. Para encontrar un registro superior hay que remontarse a la temporada 1940-41, cuando el Sevilla alcanzó los 32 goles en sus seis primeros encuentros, aunque con un matiz importante: el conjunto hispalense ganó cuatro de esos seis partidos y el Barça ha hecho pleno de triunfos. Aquel Sevilla contaba con una nómina de futbolistas como Campanal I, López, Raimundo, Pepillo, Torrontegui, Berrocal, Félix, Villalonga, Cayuso y Alcázar. En la primera jornada, el Sevilla goleó al Barcelona por 11-1 y, en la tercera, volvió a desatarse con diez tantos contra el Valencia. Pese a semejante arranque, el conjunto sevillista no mantuvo el ritmo durante toda la competición. De esos seis primeros encuentros únicamente ganó cuatro y terminó la temporada en quinta posición, con 70 goles a favor en 22 jornadas. Su promedio final fue de 3,1 tantos por cruce, muy por debajo de la velocidad anotadora que había mostrado durante aquel espectacular inicio. El Barcelona de Hansi Flick ha superado registros que llevaban décadas vigentes en la entidad azulgrana. El anterior techo culé después de las seis primeras jornadas estaba situado en 23 goles, una cifra que se había alcanzado en las temporadas 2011-12 y 1950-51. Ahora, el equipo ha añadido cinco más a esa marca y ha elevado el récord hasta los 28. La voracidad ofensiva del Barcelona no se limita al número de goles. El equipo también está demostrando una capacidad especial para golpear muy pronto a sus rivales. Los aficionados azulgranas tienen motivos para estar pendientes desde el primer minuto del partido de su equipo, porque en los últimos cuatro encuentros el bloque ha celebrado la primera diana antes de que se cumpliera el minuto diez. Contra el Valencia, Lamine Yamal marcó en el 6'. Contra el Feyenoord, Raphinha adelantó al Barcelona en el 3'. En el Ciutat de València, Xavi Espart inauguró el marcador en el 5' y, contra el Racing el miércoles por la noche, Cancelo puso el 1-0 en el 8'. Hay otro dato que refuerza todavía más la regularidad ofensiva del equipo. En todos esos encuentros, el Barcelona ha conseguido marcar tanto en la primera como en la segunda parte. Es decir, todavía no ha dejado una mitad completa sin celebrar un gol. El resultado es un equipo que ha comenzado la temporada a un ritmo goleador extraordinario. 28 goles en seis jornadas sitúan al Barcelona ante un registro que no se veía desde hace 86 años y que, de mantenerse, amenaza con convertir este inicio de curso en uno de los más productivos de toda la historia.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso: Chelsea manager says Blues needed 'an update' rather than a reset when he took over at Stamford Bridge
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Xabi Alonso discusses Chelsea's summer "update", why he's not looking for perfection, when to judge his Blues side and more; watch Chelsea vs Brentford live on Sky Sports Premier League from 7pm on Friday; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
The 44-year-old signed a four-year contract in May and took over a Blues side that finished 10th in the Premier League, after parting ways with both Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior during a tumultuous campaign at Stamford Bridge.

That meant missing out on European football for the third time in four seasons.

"Not a reset - it was an update, I would say. To change or to take decisions in another direction," he said in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports .

"My main concern is the squad, the team, the players that we have, in which stage of their career they are, in which moments we want to bring them, what we have, what we can improve.

"Those were, for me, the important decisions, the important things to analyse before coming here. Once we agreed we wanted to take one direction, it was about taking decisions.

"Some of them we took, others will have to be taken, but we are convinced with all of them.

"Now it's competition time. It's not about improving, now it's with the team that we have to work hard, improve, knowing that we have to learn from mistakes, from the good things as well, and we are in that moment."

Alonso has taken charge of six games in all competitions so far; two wins, one draw and a defeat in the league and two wins from two in the Carabao Cup.

Next up, his Chelsea side make the short trip to the Gtech Community Stadium to take on Brentford in a west London derby on Friday night, which is live on Sky Sports .

"If I look for perfection, I will be frustrated always," he said.

"What I'm looking for is to reach a good level, good continuity, good solidity; to be a team that knows what they're going to do and have this confidence and this conviction whenever you are facing any opposition.

"We are in the process. We will get there when some processes are quicker or longer, but we are working to have that feeling and when you see that we are going on the pitch we have that belief that we know what we are going to do.

"The early days are just for games and I'm not that focused about the other teams. I'm very focused about my own team and all my players and the development that we will do, the process and the improvement that we have to make.

"We need to learn quick because the competition is furious in the Premier League and I'm sure that the Chelsea of the first day and the Chelsea of the last day in the Premier League will be different and I'm sure that it will be better. It will be getting better and better with weeks and with games."

Asked when people should just his team, he added: "It's not for me to answer.

"I prefer not to ask things from people. I prefer to do things.

"And knowing that, I am aware everything takes time in football, but time will tell."

Alonso: Joao Pedro could feature for Chelsea vs Brentford

Alonso has said Joao Pedro could feature against Brentford on Friday Night Football - despite pulling out of the Brazil squad with injury.

it was announced on Wednesday night that Pedro has withdrawn from the Brazil squad - raising concerns about his fitness levels as Chelsea look to get back to winning ways.

"In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad, we are having the last training session [on Friday]," Alonso said.

"No one is ruled out. I remain cautious and we wait. We will see [on Friday] if he's ready to play. We will take a decision."

Asked what he can say about Pedro's injury issues, Alonso simply replied: "No."

Asked if he could play against Brentford on Friday, but then not play for Brazil, Alonso said: "It is a possibility."

Then asked if Pedro is disappointed to be missing out of Brazil, especially given he was not selected for the World Cup, Alonso replied: "He has moved on from the summer, he has moved on from the World Cup.

"He has shown this desire, determination to have a great season so far. The summer is far away now.

"He will be [in the Brazil squad] in the future. I'm pretty sure he is going to be."

articles.title: Expert CFB Betting Locks for Ole Miss vs. LSU and Week 3's Biggest Games
articles.summary: No matter how much we think we know, and no matter how much time and energy we spend to leap to these conclusions, sometimes (well, oftentimes) we're reminded how strange and magnificent college football can be.
articles.body:
No matter how much we think we know, and no matter how much time and energy we spend to leap to these conclusions, sometimes (well, oftentimes) we're reminded how strange and magnificent college football can be.

Everything about this roster seemed special. The quarterback, the defense, the weapons. Then the season began.

In two games, the Ducks nearly lost as a 25.5-point favorite then lost outright as a 23.5-point favorite. For what it's worth, we weren't on either of those plays. We did, however, predict that Oregon would win the national championship.

Needless to say, that isn't looking great.

Things move fast, and they will continue to move fast. Week 3 features one of the sport's most anticipated games and a slew of matchups that could serve as launchpads for hopeful teams.

As for us, we could use a launchpad. Things aren't great; things aren't bad. Picks have been hovering around .500 thus far, although a stretch of winning weeks is coming.

Our copy for this section was long submitted when LSU listed QB Sam Leavitt as "doubtful" for the game with an upper body injury on the injury report on Wednesday night.

It is indeed a talking point, likely as his coach intended, although we will remain convinced he's playing until further notice.

We could be right, we could be wrong. It doesn't change our stance either way. (Spoiler alert.)

It can be challenging to handicap an environment's true impact on a point spread, especially in college football, although the setting of this matchup will certainly have a sizable impact on what happens come Saturday night.

Lane Kiffin's team started slowly against Louisiana Tech in Week 2 before turning it on in the second half. What exactly does it tell us? It could have been a massive football hangover after a thrilling Week 1; it could be that Clemson, which produced another lackluster showing in Week 2, might simply be bad.

Either way, LSU's rebuilt roster will hit the road for the first time, taking on one of the most hostile scenes the sport has seen in some time. Given the way Kiffin left the program, those surveying the broadcast for obscene language and gestures should be on guard.

As for the game itself, the legs of both quarterbacks will likely help decide it. Trinidad Chambliss and Sam Leavitt are both exceptional at extending plays and causing chaos, and this will be a matchup loaded with potential broken, successful plays.

Will LSU be the more public side here? It's hard to know after a bit of a lackluster Week 2, but one of the early darlings of college football will certainly garner plenty of support.

This is a Chambliss pick. It's that simple. The QB has taken over many games since being thrust into this role, and he could do it again here.

Do we feel great about this? Not particularly.

Supporting a team that was throttled by UMass in the past month doesn't exactly ooze excellence. Not to mention, USC enters Week 3 with plenty of buzz and some young players emerging quickly.

But timing matters, and the timing of this football game is particularly interesting.

In Week 4, the Trojans will welcome the struggling Oregon Ducks into town—a game that could be monumental for Lincoln Riley's program. A cross-country trip to New Jersey in advance of such a massive game is a brilliant bit of scheduling.

It's also worth noting that this will serve as the Trojans' first road game of the year, meaning many of this team's young players—and there are some really good ones on offense—will have to recalibrate some.

For Rutgers, it must first limit turnovers. AJ Surace showed promise in his first start last week; he also threw four interceptions. If the Scarlet Knights can limit mistakes and get the ball to wideout KJ Duff, it could make this one weirder than it should be.

No matter what we've seen transpire over these first few weeks, the point spread is difficult to digest.

North Carolina, program turmoil and all, is 2-0 and just a small road underdog against Clemson, a team that was regularly competing for national championships not terribly long ago.

But given everything we've seen from the Tigers in two short lackluster weeks, it's not necessarily wrong.

Dabo Swinney has officially named Tait Reynolds the starter at quarterback for this matchup. The 19-year-old was thrust into the game against Georgia Southern when Christopher Vizzina was injured.

It'll be Reynolds' show for the foreseeable future, which promises to feature highs and certainly some lows. Going up against Bill Belichick, the man who used to create gameplans to slow down Peyton Manning, will be fascinating.

As for the Tar Heels, they come into this game at 2-0. While the offense will be a work in progress, QB Billy Edwards Jr. gives them plenty of experience and a chance.

A total in the low-to-mid 40s tells the story. This will be an ugly football game that UNC wins, which could spell a much different discussion at Clemson.

For the first time this year—but certainly not the last—we're fading a team in consecutive weeks.

It's not personal, Vanderbilt. Just business.

Last week, we liked Delaware +20.5, and the Blue Hens made a game of it late to easily stay within that number. This week, we're back on North Carolina State, which clobbered Richmond after an ugly loss against Virginia in Week 0.

There's no sugarcoating it. That loss was grotesque in all areas. Quarterback CJ Bailey wasn't great, and neither was his defense. Rather than overreact, however, we're properly reacting.

As for Vanderbilt, things are a work in progress. The Commodores have played Austin Peay and Delaware, and they haven't looked particularly solid in either game. Freshman QB Jared Curtis looks like a future star, but he's about to see speed he's never seen in his entire life.

The Wolfpack burned us a few weeks ago, but we're not losing faith. Bailey showcases why he's a player worth watching with a (small) upset win.

On the topic of teams that were featured in last week's selections, enter Arizona State.

If you were to look at the final score of last week's game against Texas A&M, you wouldn't care much for what you saw. Needless to say, getting 14.5 points, we weren't thrilled with the 48-20 final score.

The box score, however, tells a slightly different story. ASU outgained A&M by more than 100 yards, and the game was relatively close until late. Four Arizona State turnovers and two defensive touchdowns, however, ultimately flipped the script for the Aggies.

Needless to say, this was an agonizing watch for backers.

With that acknowledged, ASU did plenty of things well. The offense had plenty of good moments, and wideout Reed Harris is becoming a star before our eyes.

Kansas, meanwhile, had its own implosion against Missouri. QB Isaiah Marshall looked overwhelmed, and playing on the road against a capable team one week later might not help.

The Jayhawks also gave up nearly 500 yards on defense. Yikes.

Both teams come in licking their wounds, although Arizona State seems more positioned for a proper rebound.

As a reminder, we're playing in England. That variable will create some intrigue and unknowns, although it doesn't change how we feel.

Given how dominant North Texas was against UNLV on Saturday, this line will surprise some. Don't let the 0-2 mark fool you, though. This Texas State team has both talent and offense, and it'll finally show in Week 3.

This is a bit of a sandwich game for BYU, which just delivered an impressive conference win over Arizona. Next week, the Cougars are back on the road at TCU. Before then, Colorado State is poised to make this a little too close for comfort.

Things get real for James Franklin in a hurry. Sure, Virginia Tech is 2-0, and a revenge win over Old Dominion is by no means a bad win. A road trip to Maryland with a revamped roster, however, is a game that should cause some trouble.

This is not a game that typically finds its way into these picks, although we've seen enough of Northern Illinois to make an exception. Plus, despite the loss to BYU last week, Arizona showed a ton. This will be very ugly.

articles.title: Steve Belichick resigns as North Carolina's defensive coordinator
articles.summary: Belichick has been on medical leave since early August.
articles.body:
Steve Belichick is out as North Carolina's defensive coordinator as the school announced it has concluded its investigation into the program's "culture and climate."

Belichick's resignation will be official as of Oct. 27, which marks the end of a medical leave that he has been on since Aug. 6. His exit follows that of general manager Mike Lombardi, who resigned on Sept. 3 following an investigation over allegations related to a human resources dispute involving a former school front-office employee.

"The University has concluded a thorough and independent investigation into the allegations related to culture and climate within the Carolina football program," the school wrote in a statement. "The investigation determined that certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina's values and standards of conduct. articles.title: El PSG, a Marsella sin su gente
articles.standfirst: Las autoridades francesas han prohibido viajar a los aficionados del conjunto parisino
articles.summary: Las autoridades francesas han prohibido viajar a los aficionados del conjunto parisino
articles.body: Los hinchas del Paris Saint-Germain tienen prohibido viajar a Marsella debido al riesgo de enfrentamientos violentos entre seguidores con motivo del partido más trascendental del fútbol francés el domingo, informaron las autoridades locales. Los "ultra" más radicales del Paris Saint-Germain señalaron que han iniciado una acción legal para impugnar la decisión antes del partido de la Ligue 1 en el estadio Velódrome. "Estamos pidiendo a nuestro abogado que presente un procedimiento de urgencia ante el Consejo de Estado con el fin de impugnar la próxima prohibición ministerial", dijo el Collectif Ultras Paris. "Desde 2015, seis prefectos se han sucedido, sin que jamás se haya establecido con nosotros un diálogo real. Once años de prohibiciones repetidas no pueden sustituir al diálogo". En Francia, a los aficionados visitantes se les prohíbe con regularidad asistir a partidos de alto riesgo, y es poco probable que la acción legal de los seguidores del PSG prospere. Para justificar la prohibición de viajar, el Ministerio del Interior de Francia insistió en que las relaciones entre los aficionados del Marsella y del PSG han sido hostiles durante muchos años. Recordó incidentes ocurridos en París en febrero de 2018, durante el partido más reciente al que asistieron seguidores de ambos equipos, cuando ocho agentes del orden resultaron heridos. El partido entre el PSG y el Marsella se conoce como "Le Classique". El enfrentamiento se popularizó durante la década de 1990, cuando la llegada de jugadores destacados a ambos clubes avivó la rivalidad. El Marsella, el primer equipo francés en ganar la Liga de Campeones en 1993, se ha quedado muy atrás desde que el PSG fue adquirido por inversores cataríes en 2011, pero el encuentro sigue despertando pasión. El vigente campeón PSG está dos puntos por encima del Marsella, que ha tenido dificultades tras no poder fichar a ningún jugador durante el verano debido a limitaciones financieras.

articles.title: Eric García: "Ojalá la próxima temporada nos encontremos para celebrar la Champions"
articles.standfirst: Martorell homenajeó e impuso la medalla al mérito deportivo al defensa tras ganar el Mundial
articles.summary: Martorell homenajeó e impuso la medalla al mérito deportivo al defensa tras ganar el Mundial
articles.body: Eric García recibió este jueves el cariño y el reconocimiento de su ciudad natal, Martorell. El consistorio homenajeó al defensa y le impuso la medalla al mérito deportivo tras ganar el pasado verano el Mundial. También inauguró dos campos Cruyff Courts en la localidad. Sin duda, la tarde de este 17 de septiembre quedará en la memoria de Eric García. A primera hora, fue recibido institucionalmente en el Ayuntamiento y, posteriormente, se dirigió a los ciudadanos de Martorell desde el balcón del consistorio. "Es una tarde especial para mí, es un privilegio estar aquí, en el lugar que me ha visto crecer. Pude levantar la Copa del Mundo con mis compañeros. Veo a muchos niños aquí que seguro que su sueño es el mismo que yo tuve, llegar a ser jugador. A veces los sueños se hacen realidad", dijo el defensa. Además, Eric García también lanzó un guiño al Barcelona. "Veo también muchas camisetas azulgranas por aquí. Ojalá la próxima temporada nos encontremos para celebrar muchos títulos y ojalá la Champions", concluyó el defensa. Tras esta parte de carácter más institucional, el zaguero se desplazó al Parc de la Vila para inaugurar dos pistas de Cruyff Courts y repasar la actualidad azulgrana. "La Champions es el gran objetivo de todos. Los dos últimos años hemos hecho las cosas bien, pero nos quedamos fuera. Este año tenemos una gran plantilla y, si seguimos a este nivel, podemos estar arriba. La Champions es un sueño de todos", reiteró. Además, el defensa se sumó a la petición de que Lamine Yamal sea Balón de Oro. "Se lo merece. Todos lo decimos porque lo sentimos. Las cosas que hace... yo vi a Messi y ahora a él... La edad que tiene, lo diferencial que es en el campo, tiene una calidad increíble. Pero tampoco me quiero olvidar de mis compañeros. Como Rodri ya tiene uno... (risas)", reflexionó. Por último, el defensa habló de Szczesny. "Es una persona con mucha experiencia dentro del fútbol. Obviamente, ser el suplente no es fácil. Joan es el mejor portero del mundo", concluyó.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea ambitions ‘very clear’ as Boehly era ends
articles.summary: Chelsea announce that Clearlake will acquire the stakes of Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said Chelsea’s ambition was “very clear” after Clearlake Capital took full control of the Premier League club, ending Todd Boehly’s chairmanship.

Chelsea announced late on Wednesday that Clearlake, led by co-founders Behdad Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano, would acquire the stakes of Boehly and director Mark Walter.

US billionaires Boehly and Walter partnered with Clearlake to buy the London club from Roman Abramovich in May 2022 in a sale mandated by the British government.

Prior to the new deal, private equity company Clearlake had owned 61.5 percent of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss.

Chelsea said Wyss would “remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group”.

Boehly and Walter are among the co-owners of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, while Walter recently sold the Los Angeles Lakers basketball franchise for $12.5bn.

The Financial Times reported that the pair were set to receive 950 million pounds ($1.27bn) for their combined stakes in Chelsea, in a deal that values the club at about five billion pounds, including debt.

In a new statement on Thursday, Chelsea said: “Our ambition is clear: to compete at the highest level, to win major trophies, and to build sustained success”.

Blues boss Alonso, who started at Chelsea on July 1 , told reporters that the change was “an important day for the club”.

“Thanks to the former owners for what they’ve done. I was not here, but I know they played an important role,” he said on the eve of Chelsea’s Premier League match at Brentford on Friday.

“And now that Behdad is taking more control, almost full control, I think it’s good that the main one is clear.

“I have very good relations with Behdad. He was the one that came to Madrid to explain to me the project, to convince me and we are working well together.”

“We know where we want to be, we know that everything takes time, but the ambition for that is very clear,” the Spaniard added.

Since the takeover in 2022, Chelsea’s highest Premier League finish is fourth in 2024/25, when the club won the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup.

Former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen coach Alonso has a brief to revitalise the underachieving Chelsea squad, which finished a dismal 10th in the Premier League last season.

The Blues have made a mixed start to the new campaign, taking seven points from their four Premier League games to sit sixth in the table.

Boehly and Walter have also sold their stakes in Chelsea’s partner club, French Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, giving full control to Clearlake.

articles.title: England squad: Will Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold be left out again after World Cup snubs?
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel is set to name his first England squad since the World Cup on Friday; having stated publicly that England's DNA does not allow for ball-retaining passers, can he continue to leave the likes of Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold out?
articles.body:
Palmer, along with Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold , was a headline omission from Thomas Tuchel's tournament squad in May, but he is one of the most startlingly in-form players in the Premier League right now, and the smart money is on him winning his international place back.

In the hugely oversubscribed No 10 role, the England boss went with Jude Bellingham , Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze in May, but Palmer is now fully fit after groin problems limited him to just 26 appearances last season, and his form has flourished.

Two goals and two assists show that. Only his team-mate Joao Pedro has more in the Premier League so far this season and only Bruno Fernandes has created more chances and had more shots combined (25) than Palmer (24).

It also feels like a space may have opened up for Palmer, with Eze's indifferent form for Arsenal. While starting in Europe and the Carabao Cup, Eze has yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.

Morgan Gibbs-White is in with a shout, after an impressive start to the campaign. But Tuchel constantly talks about "connections" between players as the key to England's success, and right now it is hard to argue there is a better attacking connection in the Premier League than Palmer and his close friend Rogers. There certainly is not an all-English one.

Will Tuchel try to change England 'DNA'?

This squad selection will be the first staging post in Tuchel's brave new post-World Cup era. Having stated publicly that England's DNA does not allow for ball-retaining passers, can he continue to leave Palmer, Foden and Alexander-Arnold in exile - three generational talents in terms of their passing and attacking prowess?

The issue here is that Tuchel is not a man to admit he was wrong. Like many, if not all, of the very best coaches in the world, there is an in-built self-belief - an arrogance, some would say - which is very hard to shake. It is partly what gives him his aura.

And if Tuchel does recall one of those big three, does that show the mask is slipping? Plenty in the media will pounce and take it as proof that the England boss got it wrong on the biggest stage when he named his World Cup squad three months ago. But he will also be criticised if he leaves those superstars out again. It is a lose-lose.

Despite his sending off in the Manchester derby last weekend, Foden has started the season in fine form. He leads the Premier League in assists after a ball carry (2), alongside Cody Gakpo and Julio Enciso. And of all the English players at Tuchel's disposal, he is probably the most technically adept with the ball at his feet. It remains to be seen whether Foden fits into the England plans right now.

Alexander-Arnold may struggle to force his way back in, despite the glaring right-back issues Tuchel faced at the World Cup. Reece James and Tino Livramento both suffered injuries, leaving many to lament the Real Madrid star's absence, especially when centre-back Trevoh Chalobah was called up as a late replacement for Livramento instead.

But Tuchel has been adamant that the former Liverpool full-back's profile does not suit how he wants his England side to play, and it would be a big shift in the manager's philosophy if he went back on that now.

Alexander-Arnold has started only two LaLiga games this season, yet he has managed more successful crosses than all but two defenders in the league (6).

Tuchel knows top-quality delivery comes standard with Alexander-Arnold, but the manager has always thought defensive prowess matters more.

Tuchel does have something of a defensive crisis. The absences of John Stones , Dan Burn , Djed Spence and Ben White due to injury mean there are plenty of opportunities at the back. James has also missed Chelsea training this week, but has not been ruled out.

Despite those doubts, it still feels unlikely that Harry Maguire will get the nod for an international recall. Speaking out in frustration about his World Cup omission - the day before Tuchel publicly named the squad - was not well received by the England hierarchy.

The 33-year-old has been ever-present and impressive in Manchester United's four league games so far this season. He is currently ranked third in the Premier League for ball-carrying.

Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall - another controversial omission from the World Cup squad - is expected to get the chance this time in the Nations League. His consistency is clear and he has been excellent again this season - the best in the Premier League for winning possession in the defensive third (19 times) and fifth for successful blocks (5).

Whether Maguire's United team-mate Kobbie Mainoo is included in this Nations League squad remains to be seen. He did not play a minute of football at the World Cup , and was thoroughly disillusioned by the end.

Sky Sports News expected him to be selected for the third-place play-off match, but back pain developed in the final training session before the game, ruling him out. Nevertheless, his form for Manchester United so far has made him a strong England candidate.

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is pushing hard for a recall after an explosive start to the season. His double against Newcastle on Monday means it is four goals in six games so far.

It is form Tuchel cannot ignore, especially since Calvert-Lewin's main rival Ollie Watkins is now playing in the Saudi Pro League. Watkins' move to Al Hilal has seen him start in sparkling form, however, with three goals and two assists in four appearances.

Ivan Toney , who was the surprise inclusion at the World Cup, is unlikely to be considered for selection this time. He is due to be in court in Westminster in the middle of the international break to answer charges of assault causing actual bodily harm. His lawyer says he is looking forward to the opportunity to clear his name.

Despite the excitement around Max Dowman's performances for Arsenal and his two goals in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, no one expects an early call-up to the senior squad. The 16-year-old has not yet played for England's U21s, which is a more likely route as the FA, similarly to Mikel Arteta, carefully manage his minutes and his progression.

Dean Henderson has a foot injury, meaning there is space for a third goalkeeper to be called up alongside the guaranteed Jordan Pickford and James Trafford .

articles.title: Wrexham owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac aim Spygate dig at Southampton
articles.summary: Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have poked fun at next opponents Southampton ahead of their Championship fixture this weekend.
articles.body:
Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have taken a light-hearted jab at this weekend's opponents Southampton by referencing the Spygate saga in a cheeky social media post.

The Saints visit their Championship rivals at the Racecourse Ground on Saturday (15:00 BST) and the Hollywood duo did not miss their chance to make light of last season's play-off drama.

Southampton were kicked out of the play-off final and docked four points after an intern was found observing semi-final opponents Middlesbrough in training, with similar incidents later found to have taken place at Oxford United and Ipswich Town earlier in the campaign.

Wrexham's A-list duo appeared in a video on Wrexham's X account, which started with Reynolds emerging from behind a tree.

In a skit nominally aimed at promoting shirt sponsor Firefox, Deadpool star Reynolds says: "Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy."

It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Mac adds: "Specifically, how to prevent spies from seeing what you're doing."

Discussing internet safety, Reynolds jokes about searching for "how to run a football club" before the pair declare privacy is "important to people everywhere", specifically name-checking Middlesbrough, Oxford and Ipswich.

Reynolds concludes by saying: "Refreshing, huh? An organisation that actually respects your privacy."

The 59-second clip ends with the pair looking at a mobile phone, purportedly showing a Southampton pickleball team in practice.

Wrexham's Broadhead to miss Wales games with injury

Parkinson's 'wriggle room' as Wrexham seek response

When announcing their league fixtures for the current campaign in June, Wrexham took another gentle swipe at the Saints.

On their September schedule, the club had written "check training ground" along with an asterisk that clarified "for unauthorised visitors" on the date of 17 September, two days prior to their contest with Southampton .

Wrexham sit 19th in the table after seven games, with Southampton ninth on 10 points, three more than the north Wales outfit.

Tonda Eckert's men won 5-1 against Wrexham on their most recent visit to the Racecourse Ground in April as they overtook the Welsh side and went on to clinch a play-off spot.

Amid the uncertainty around Spygate , Wrexham kept in contact with the English Football League (EFL) following the conclusion of the 2025-26 regular season.

But Parkinson said his side's sole focus now lies on delivering a positive display against the Saints this weekend following their 6-0 loss to West Ham United last time out.

"We're the team which obviously were affected because we were seventh, but we accepted the EFL decision on that," said Parkinson.

" Southampton got punished for it and they've had to accept their punishment and move on.

"That's all I can say on it really, it's gone. We're concentrating on what we've got to do and likewise they're the same."

articles.title: Texas' Steve Sarkisian Addresses Controversy on Holly Rowe, Arch Manning and AI ESPN Video
articles.summary: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian on Thursday addressed the recent controversy involving quarterback Arch Manning and an AI video featuring ESPN's Holly Rowe.
articles.body:
Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian on Thursday addressed the recent controversy involving quarterback Arch Manning and an AI video featuring ESPN's Holly Rowe.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Sarkisian called the situation an "unfortunate" mistake and that no one involved with the Texas program condones domestic violence or violence against women:

"We know we're going to have more opportunities with that crew covering us, and we're looking forward to those opportunities. So, [I] could have definitely handled that situation better with a little bit more patience in the moment. But that obviously led to the situation with Arch and his press conference as it pertained to the AI video, and obviously Arch recognizes he made a mistake, and it's an unfortunate one. Nowhere do we condone domestic violence or violence against women. Nothing in our program says that nor Arch individually.

Fanbases That Should be Worried after Week 2 😨

"I think if he could take it back, he would. But he has since apologized to Holly. He's made a public apology, and you know our goal is that we can move forward and him be the guy that that we all know that he is and what he represents."

On the heels of Texas' 24-23 win over Ohio State last weekend, Manning was asked during a press conference on Monday if he had seen any social media posts from the victory.

"I've seen a few AI edits, that's about it. I saw an AI edit of Sark's interview," Manning answered . "Y'all seen that one? That's a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe. It's hilarious."

Amid criticism about those comments, Manning issued an apology to Rowe on his Instagram Story.

Rowe, who was the sideline reporter for ESPN's coverage of the OSU-Texas game, replied on social media by writing that she and Manning had a private conversation about the situation and she accepted his apology.

After Texas' dramatic comeback win that saw it score 21 points in the fourth quarter to erase a 20-point deficit, Rowe attempted to interview Sarkisian on the field. She started to ask a question when Sarkisian yelled, "Let's go, Texas fight! Let's go, Texas, fight!" and put up the "Hook 'Em" sign with his hand before walking away.

It was the second time in the game that an ESPN sideline reporter was unable to get an interview with Sarkisian.

Laura Rutledge attempted to speak to Sarkisian at halftime, but she explained on the broadcast they were having technical issues and he was "very patient" in waiting "a long time" before needing to go the locker room to address his team.

Texas currently has three more games scheduled to air on the ABC/ESPN family of networks this season, including the next two weeks against UTSA (SEC Network) and Tennessee (ABC).

articles.title: Bill Belichick Calls Out 'Ridiculous' Rumors on Jordon Hudson's Role with UNC Football Team
articles.summary: UNC head coach Bill Belichick is clearing the air about his girlfriend Jordon Hudson's involvement with the football team.
articles.body:
UNC head coach Bill Belichick is clearing the air about his girlfriend Jordon Hudson's involvement with the football team.

Speaking to Allie Jones of The Wall Street Journal , Belichick called out the narratives that have suggested that Hudson pursued an official role with the Tar Heels.

"The way the story was picked up was a long way from that," he said. "Like, 'She's trying to be the general manager of the team,' and it's so ridiculous."

Fanbases That Should be Worried after Week 2 😨

The 74-year-old Belichick has long faced scrutiny for his relationship with the 25-year-old Hudson. During Belichick's first season as UNC head coach, Hudson's influence came under the spotlight when she interrupted his interview with CBS Sunday Morning multiple times.

Still, Belichick explained to Jones that Hudson has been assisting him with other aspects of his career that don't pertain to the Tar Heels.

"When I took the job here, it was December, and at that time I was doing five TV shows, the radio show, I had a book coming out," Belichick said. "I had a lot of other things going on when I took the job."

He continued: "So, I sent an email when I got here and I said, Can you please forward any requests to Jordon about my personal appearances so that I can work and coordinate them outside the university? Didn't have anything to do with the university. Well, that was leaked as released as 'Jordon's involved in every single thing that I do and she's copied on every email.' That's just a flat-out lie."

When asked to describe his current working relationship with Hudson, Belichick said, "There are some things that she helps me schedule or look at. It's not North Carolina stuff."

Belichick and the Tar Heels are off to a 2-0 start this season and will face Clemson (1-1) on Saturday.

articles.summary: El Andorra tiene plena confianza en el crecimiento y el potencial del joven serbio y lo aumenta su vinculación hasta el 2030
articles.body: Después de blindar el juvenil Tiago Olmedo, el Andorra ha hecho lo mismo con Stefan Golubović, también hasta el año 2030. Con sólo 20 años, el serbio sigue dando pasos adelante dentro del proyecto tricolor después de una gran temporada cedido en el Cornellà, donde marcó cinco goles, y de incorporarse este verano a la dinámica. De hecho, en el primer partido liguero de esta temporada, el contundente triunfo ante el Ceuta, salió de inicio. En este sentido, el club liderado en los despachos por Gerard Piqué ha mencionado en un comunicado que "confía en el crecimiento de Golubović y en su potencial" para que siga desarrollándose con la camiseta pirenaica en las próximas temporadas. Tanto es así que, aunque en Vigo no jugó, si lo hizo durante 10 minutos contra el Eibar, toda la segunda mitad de Valladolid y repitiendo titularidad contra la Real Sociedad B. Desde su llegada, Golubović asegura haberse adaptado rápidamente y se ha mostrado muy satisfecho con la renovación: "Estoy muy contento de que se haya confiado en mí durante otros cuatro años. Creo que puede ser una historia muy buena para mí y el club". El delantero ha destacado también el cambio que ha vivido en los últimos tiempos: "Hace dos años estaba en Serbia pensando incluso en dejar el fútbol y ahora estoy en Segunda División española, una de las mejores segundas del mundo".

articles.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin adds goals to become one of Premier League's most complete strikers - The Radar
articles.summary: Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, described as "unplayable" by Jamie Carragher, is the focus of The Radar column as he pushes for an England recall; plus: Brian Brobbey's unmatched hold-up play for Sunderland and Elliot Anderson's Rodri impression for Man City
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Calvert-Lewin's all-round threat 🔺Brobbey the hold-up master 🔺Anderson filling Rodri's shoes 🔺A player to watch this weekend

It took an assist from the goal accreditation appeals panel but Dominic Calvert-Lewin is up to three goals for the season in the Premier League. His revised total puts him behind only Manchester City's Erling Haaland. He is in the frame for an England recall.

Factor all competitions and it is nine goals in 15 appearances for Calvert-Lewin since April. "He is in outstanding shape and playing with lots of confidence," said Leeds boss Daniel Farke after the striker's starring display in Monday's 4-1 win over Newcastle.

Calvert-Lewin has always had a knack for getting into the right positions. His shot maps, both at Leeds and for his final two seasons at Everton, show a concentration of efforts from the centre of the box. The difference is that he is now converting more of them.

Calvert-Lewin's wastefulness came to define him at Everton. But he has already scored as many Premier League goals for Leeds as he managed in his final four seasons there. "Sometimes a move rejuvenates a player," said Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

The underlying data illustrates how the gap between his expected goals and actual goals scored has narrowed as he has gradually emerged from his finishing funk. "Maybe sometimes composure has let him down in his career, but not here," added Carragher.

His goals against Newcastle showed the breadth of his attacking threat. First, a characteristic leap and header to dispatch James Justin's cross. Then, a darting run in behind to reach Tarik Muharemovic's first-time pass and finish beyond the goalkeeper.

Farke described him as "one of the standout strikers in the league" after the game. Now that he has rediscovered his cutting edge in front of goal, it is difficult to argue otherwise.

The 29-year-old offers that coveted blend of speed and aerial strength. Monday's game was another reminder of how he can dominate centre-backs from long passes and crosses, while also making runs to stretch opponents and threaten in behind.

His completeness as a No 9 can also be seen in the numbers.

Calvert-Lewin is joint-top with Sunderland defender Dan Ballard for aerials won in the Premier League this season and stands out as the only player near the top of that list who also ranks among the top 10 players in the division for runs in behind.

Tracking data shows he has clocked one of the highest top speeds in the Premier League this season. His off-the-ball intensity is invaluable to Leeds defensively as well as offensively. "It's not just scoring goals," added Farke on Monday. "His work-rate is top."

Calvert-Lewin continues to lead the press for Leeds, shutting down opposition defenders, blocking passing lanes, and helping his side steal possession in dangerous areas. Only six sides have forced more high turnovers than Leeds since the start of last term.

Availability is of course another huge factor in Calvert-Lewin's resurgence. His injury record made his signing a gamble for Leeds, even on a free transfer. But he has so far avoided any recurrence of the issues that plagued him at Everton.

Leeds have managed his minutes where possible. Farke has substituted him in 15 of his 34 Premier League starts. But he played nearly 80 per cent of Premier League minutes last season, his highest ratio since 2020/21, and has played 92 per cent this term.

The consistency of selection has benefitted all parties and Leeds will hope for more of the same when Crystal Palace visit Elland Road, live on Sky Sports on Sunday, with Calvert-Lewin aiming to score for a sixth consecutive Premier League home game.

On current form it would be foolish to bet against him.

From one striker capable of throwing his weight around to another in Brian Brobbey. The Netherlands international, scorer of three goals at the World Cup, is yet to find the net for Sunderland this term but faces Manchester City, live on Sky Sports on Sunday, having served up a masterclass in hold-up play against Arsenal.

His running battle with Ezri Konsa was a sight to behold. Brobbey repeatedly pinned the Arsenal centre-back, showing incredible strength to retain possession from long passes and giving Sunderland an invaluable means of getting up the pitch.

It is an area in which Brobbey is uniquely gifted. According to GeniusIQ , he has recorded more hold-ups, defined as instances of a player using their body to shield a defender from the ball to retain possession, than anyone else this season. He topped the rankings last term too, despite only starting 22 games.

The goals are yet to flow for him but Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris is delighted with his striker. "The game against Arsenal shows that even against the strongest teams in the league or in Europe, he is really competitive," he said this week.

Sunderland will need a repeat performance at the Etihad Stadium.

Elliot Anderson will be one of the players tasked with cutting off the supply line to Brobbey on Sunday. The early evidence suggests the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest is up to the task of filling the void left by Rodri in Manchester City's midfield.

In fact, the 23-year-old, outstanding in last weekend's Manchester derby win at Old Trafford, is making an almost identical number of passes and passes in the final third as Rodri last season, while also winning an almost identical number of duels. The likenesses have so far made for a smooth transition under Enzo Maresca.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Could Fulham inflict more misery on Manchester United on Sunday? They are yet to win a Premier League game under Alvaro Arbeloa but in Josh King they have a fantastic young player in fine form.

Four Premier League games will be shown live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Brentford vs Chelsea on Friday night.

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry is live on Saturday, before four more games are shown on Sunday, with Bournemouth vs Liverpool , Leeds vs Crystal Palace and Man City vs Sunderland taking place at 2pm before Fulham vs Man Utd at 4.30pm.

Last week's column revealed the numbers behind the on-pitch understanding between Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer's . Bournemouth's Alex Scott also featured, as did Crystal Palace's Anan Khalaili before his goal against Ipswich.

articles.title: El Atlético sella el compromiso con ERGO | DKV antes del derbi madrileño
articles.standfirst: Enrique Cerezo, junto a Theo Kokkalas, CEO de ERGO International, y Fernando Campos, CEO de DKV Seguros, celebraron un encuentro institucional en el Riyadh Air Metropolitano que ratifica el acuerdo estratégico con la empresa aseguradora.
articles.summary: Enrique Cerezo, junto a Theo Kokkalas, CEO de ERGO International, y Fernando Campos, CEO de DKV Seguros, celebraron un encuentro institucional en el Riyadh Air Metropolitano que ratifica el acuerdo estratégico con la empresa aseguradora.
articles.body: El Atlético y la aseguradora ERGO | DKV ratificaron ayer su acuerdo estratégico a través de un encuentro institucional que reunió a los máximos responsables del Grupo ERGO | DKV Seguros y el Atlético de Madrid. Por parte del Atlético participaron en el evento el presidente, Enrique Cerezo y el director general de Ingresos y Operaciones, Óscar Mayo. Por parte de ERGO | DKV, se contó con la presencia de Theo Kokkalas, CEO de ERGO International y Fernando Campos, CEO de DKV Seguros. En el terreno de juego del Riyadh Air Metropolitano se inmortalizó la fotografía de familia oficial junto a los jugadores del primer equipo Koke, Le Normand y Johnny. El acuerdo que se formalizó este verano con la aseguradora otorga a ERGO | DKV visibilidad en las equipaciones de los primeros equipos masculino y femenino y posiciona a la aseguradora como Socio Premium Oficial de la Ciudad del Deporte. Este espacio permitirá a la aseguradora reforzar su compromiso con la promoción de la salud, la prevención y el bienestar, mediante iniciativas conjuntas con los operadores del complejo y el desarrollo de soluciones aseguradoras adaptadas a las necesidades de sus usuarios. Durante el encuentro, Enrique Cerezo destacó: "Estamos muy orgullosos de unir nuestro camino al de ERGO DKV, un grupo asegurador de referencia internacional con el que compartimos valores como el esfuerzo y la superación. Esta alianza nos ayudará a seguir creciendo dentro y fuera del campo". Por su parte, Theo Kokkalas, CEO de ERGO International, señaló que "La alianza con el Atlético de Madrid representa una excelente oportunidad para seguir reforzando la presencia global de la marca ERGO, al tiempo que impulsa de forma decidida nuestro negocio de seguros de salud en España, uno de nuestros mercados prioritarios de crecimiento". Finalmente, Fernando Campos, CEO de DKV Seguros, enfatizó el valor del acuerdo para la estrategia local: "Nos unimos a una de las instituciones deportivas más emblemáticas de España, con la que compartimos un paralelismo histórico de superación. Ambos hemos recorrido un largo camino desde nuestros orígenes hasta posicionarnos en la cima de nuestros respectivos ámbitos. Esta alianza refuerza nuestro compromiso con la capital, donde queremos ser un agente activo que amplifique el impacto de la salud, la prevención y el bienestar, al tiempo que impulsamos nuestro crecimiento en todo el país".

articles.body: Mateo Sobral se ha hecho con hueco en el once titular del Celta Fortuna de Fredi Álvarez. Con 17 años acumula minutos en Segunda división, siendo de los futbolistas más jóvenes en la categoría. El mediocampista que llegó al club vigués con 7 años acumulará minutos esta temporada, en la que Hugo Burcio y Andrés Antañón se perderán muchos partidos por estar en dinámica de primer equipo. El canterano fue convocado, en las últimas horas, para disputar la UEFA Friendly Cup, que se celebrará en Nyon, desde el 22 de este mes de septiembre al 4 de octubre. Por esta convocatoria, se perderá los partidos ante Sabadell y Sporting de Gijón. No son los primeros encuentros que se pierde por este motivo esta temporada. Mateo es un futbolista en el cual su entrenador, Fredi Álvarez, y el club tienen puesta mucha confianza. Por ello sus dos últimas titularidades en Segunda división con apenas 17 años.

articles.title: Texas Assistant Coach Arrested on DWI Charge in Latest Distraction for No. 1 Longhorns
articles.summary: AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Texas defensive assistant coach Johnny Nansen was arrested on a misdemeanor driving while intoxicated charge and his status for a return to the sideline with the No. 1 Longhorns has not yet been determined, head coach Steve Sarkisian announced Thursday.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Texas defensive assistant coach Johnny Nansen was arrested on a misdemeanor driving while intoxicated charge and his status for a return to the sideline with the No. 1 Longhorns has not yet been determined, head coach Steve Sarkisian announced Thursday.

Austin police said Nansen, 52, was arrested Wednesday night after officers responded to a three-vehicle wreck about 9 p.m. Nansen was one of the drivers and officers observed "multiple clues of impairment" in standard field sobriety tests, police said, without providing details.

The short description of the arrest did not mention whether Nansen submitted to a breath test. It also not detail whether Nansen or another driver was at fault in the crash.

Sarkisian said Nansen was not at practice Thursday ahead of Saturday night's home game against UTSA. Nansen coaches inside linebackers and is co-defensive coordinator. He has been on the Texas staff since 2024.

"We're obviously disappointed, but that's all I really have on it at this time," Sarkisian said.

The arrest is the latest problem for Texas after its big come-from-behind 24-23 win over the Buckeyes that boosted Texas from No. 4 to No. 1.

Star quarterback Arch Manning was forced to apologize after publicly joking about an AI-generated video that depicted Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe. That video, and other fake clips, have surfaced after a brief and testy exchange between Sarkisian and Rowe after the game.
